Krugersdorp Murder Trial

By: Kate Barry | Paid

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
The Krugersdorp Killers stand trial for the murder of 11 people

Unique Selling Point:
Exclusive court room footage of the murder trial of a family and three friends who went on a killing spree in Krugersdorp.

Summary:
We bring you the confessions, the testimony, the heartache and legal and psychological analysis of one of the most bizarre murder cases in history. The trial is in its 4th week, but with over 300 witnesses for the prosecution, even the Judge has been asking for time out. What has happened so far? What stunning pieces of evidence have come to light?

Further information:
1. We begin with a recap of our first story: who was murdered, when and how? Who are the 5 accused, and what were their motives?
2. In June 2018, high school English teacher and mother of two Marinda Steyn pleaded guilty to all 11 murders, and was received 11 life sentences and an additional 115 years in prison. Her confession exonerated her daughter, Marcel, and friend Cecilia Steyn from any involvement in the crimes.
3. In June 2018 her son Leroux Steyn (23) also pleaded guilty to 7 murders and was sentenced to 35 years in prison with 10 suspended for turning state witness. His mother and the rest of the gang have disowned him.
4. In October 2018 Zak Valentine, Cecilia Steyn and Marcel Steyn pleaded not guilty to all charges, and so began the mammoth trial.
5. Leroux Steyn testifies about the Ministry called Electus Per Deus, led by Cecilia Steyn, what was expected and their roles within the group.He gives the Court insight into the motives, planning and execution of all the crimes, including the bombing of cars, selection of victims, their murders, the theft of money and stashing of weapons and ammunition.
6. John Barnard, a member of the gang who was previously sentenced to 25, corroborates Leroux's evidence. He gives insight to his role in the planning and execution of 7 murders.
6. We hear heartbreaking testimony from each of the families about the disappearance and subsequent loss of their loved ones.
7. A trauma counsellor called to the scene of Zak's wife's murder testifies how he showed no emotion at all, and was more concerned about the whereabouts of the cat.
8. Several friends and acquaintances testify about Cecilia Steyn's "special powers" - she is a witch, a werewolf, a vampire, can see auras, and also has several personalities that appear when she is under Satanic attack.
9. A forensic pathologist will unpack these "special powers" and how this manipulation could have influenced the group to commit such heinous crimes.

Press Release:


Carte Blanche Exclusive: Krugersdorp Murder Trial
In its fourth week, with over 300 witnesses for the prosecution, even Judge Jacob Francis has asked for time out during the Krugersdorp Murder Trial. In June this year, high school teacher and mother-of-two Marinda Steyn pleaded guilty to eleven murders, and received eleven life sentences, plus an additional 115 years in prison. Now, her three alleged accomplices stand trial. Carte Blanche brings exclusive court room footage and highlights the startling pieces of evidence that have come to light from one of the country’s most outrageous killing sprees.
Producer: Kate Barry
Presenter: Devi Sankaree Govender
Watch the trailer


Script:


KK MURDER TRIAL

V/O: In May we brought you the story of the Krugersdorp Killers: a group of family and friends accused of murdering eleven people. This gang included: Zak Valentine, a North West University graduate and former financial advisor for Discovery Life. Cecilia Steyn, a mother of two and married to a policeman; Leroux Steyn began working as Zak Valentine’s assistant after leaving school. He’s not related to Cecilia. His mother is Marinda Steyn, who was teaching English at a local high school at the time of her arrest; her daughter is Marcel Steyn. Who matriculated in 2015 with six distinctions. She was 18 when she was arrested. The 6th member of the group, John Barnard had already turned state witness for a 10-year reduction in his 30-year sentence.

V/O: They all lived together in Cosanna Flats in Krugersdorp. Group leader Cecilia Steyn was an ex-Satanist. Here she is with Marinda, as well as Zak and his late wife Mikaela Valentine. In 2012 they joined the Christian group Overcomers Through Christ, for which Cecilia wrote a course called Know Your Enemy. When she clashed with group leader Ria Grunewald, she formed her own ministry called Electus Per Deus, meaning Chosen by God.

V/O: The alleged murders began in July 2012. The first two victims were Overcomers Through Christ member Natacha Burger and her elderly neighbor Joy Boonzaier. Next, was Ria Grunewald’s mentor, Pastor Reg Bendixen. When Zak’s wife Mikaela decided to leave the group, it’s alleged that Zak put sleeping tablets in her coffee before going to work. She was then viciously stabbed to death by Marinda.

In 2015, the group started killing for money. John Barnard’s employers, Peter and Joan Meyer, were stabbed to death when it turned out they didn’t keep cash at home. Zak Valentine then faked his own death for a R3.5 million insurance pay-out from Discovery Life. Street vendor Jarod Jackson was drugged and strangled, before being burned to death in Zak’s car. In the first five months of 2016, tax consultant Glenn McGregor, insurance broker Anthony Scholefied, estate agent Kevin McAlpine and Remax agent Hanle Lategan were all strangled to death for a few thousand rands stolen from their bank cards.

Devi link: The wheels of justice started turning in May. In a surprise move Marinda Steyn pleaded guilty to all charges and appeared here in the Johannesburg High Court.

Judge: The effective sentence is 11 life sentences and 115 years imprisonment.

V/O: But in a packed court room, Marinda expressed absolutely no remorse whatsoever. She stared blankly at the families of her victims, ignoring their anger until she was led down to the cells.

On the same day an emotional Leroux Steyn entered a plea bargain with the State. He pleaded guilty to 7 of the murders, and by agreeing to turn State witness received a lesser sentence from Judge Ratha Mokgoathleng.

Judge: Effectively you are to spend 25 years, after all the charges are set to run concurrently. Ok?

V/O: But Leroux’s plea differed from Marinda’s in one important aspect: he incriminated both Cecilia and his sister Marcel, whereas Marinda exonerated them both from any involvement in the crimes.

Devi: How does the Court deal with this discrepancy between her version and Leroux’s version?

Ulrich: It’s going to be interesting to see whether the Defense is going to call Marinda, the mother, because they can.

V/O: Ulrich Roux is an experienced criminal defense lawyer.

Ulrich: If she does not testify in support of the Defense, in support of the accused’s version, then Leroux’s version will be accepted.

Devi link: This mammoth trial is now in progress: Zak, Cecilia and Marcel are in the dock. The trial is now in its fourth week. The prosecution has a list of 300 witnesses, but the first witness called was Leroux Steyn.

Gerrit: What did Accused 1 and his wife, what did they tell accused 2?

Leroux: That he had stabbed Natasha and after he had stabbed her that the old lady saw that he had stabbed her as well and that Mikeila tried to get out. She ran away, or she went outside the house. She went back to the car. That is what was said.

Gerrit: Please explain to the Court what is depicted on LLL1?

Leroux: Cecilia’s collection of knives. This was situated behind her bedroom door. I counted them, in total there over 500 knives.

Gerrit: If you look at LLL2, what is depicted on that photograph?

Leroux: It is the back of Cecilia’s bedroom door, also be-littered with pangas and machetes and knives and baseball bats, and axes.

V/O: Watched by the families, Leroux Steyn testified to Judge Jacob Francis about all the murders. With a deadpan expression he told of the 5 people he personally strangled, beginning with Jarod Jackson.

Leroux: There is a piece of rope hanging on that board, a blue piece of rope with some red tape around. Cecilia took that rope off and gave that rope to me and said you are going to be strangling him with this. Zak was driving, Jarod was sitting in the passenger seat, I was sitting behind him because I had to strangle him after he took the medication and passed out. I put the rope over the seat and then I put it around his neck and I pulled tight, while we were driving. We pulled off. After pulling off we took Jarod out of the car and myself and John carried, carried him, dragged him to the Mercedes and put him in the passenger seat of the Mercedes. Myself, Zak and John threw paraffin all over the car on this inside and a bit on the outside. And then we stood away a bit and John set the car on fire.

V/O: Leroux’s testimony was corroborated by his partner in crime, convicted murderer John Barnard.

John: Zak still put his phone, put it into the driver seat, we moved the body over also into the driver seat, and then we pushed the car off the road. Once we had finished pushing the car off the road, We got paraffin, poured it all over the car and then set it alight. We then left, we went in the opposite direction for about five minutes, turned around and then drove past to make sure that the car is burning alright. Then I let Cecilia know on my phone that we were finished and we were on our way back.

Ulrich: The two State witnesses: Leroux Steyn and John Barnard who have testified, I think will be the most important witnesses for the State. Because they can corroborate each other and if they were involved in the murder, then the Defense will have to do a lot in order to disprove those allegations.

V/O: Leroux also told the Court why Cecilia needed money so badly, and why they had to keep on killing

Leroux: Cecilia was seeing a shrink.

Gerrit: A shrink, meaning? A psychologist?

Leroux: A psychologist. Ja, paying R5000 a week for her to see the shrink. She started freaking out if she can’t see the shrink, she actually started getting agitated and freaked out, and that amounted to R23 000 a month.

Devi link: The testimony of Leroux Steyn and John Barnard has finally lifted the lid on how and why the murders were committed. But for the families of the victims, it’s been difficult to listen to the matter-of-fact telling of their loved ones’ last moments.

V/O: Like the description of the murder of Glenn McGregor.

Leroux: As he turned to me it looked like he wanted to storm me, and my mother shot him twice in the back, the back, side region. After shooting him he fell to the ground. My mother went into his internet banking, she transferred R6000 from his account to hers. Then my mother told me it’s time now to kill him and that’s, that’s where it happened, where I strangled him. After strangling him, my mother said we can’t leave him in the living room because just now somebody sees him there. So my sister and myself dragged him from the living room all the way to his room in the bathroom, where he was found.

Gerrit: Your sister being Accused 3?

Leroux: Yes.

V/O: The next day Leroux drew the R6000 to give to Cecilia.

Leroux: I went and got my mother’s bank card from her while she was at work. I went and drew the money and then I took it to Cecilia. After taking it to Cecilia she sent me to Key West Nedbank to go and pay her shrink.

Giada: In his testimony one doesn’t hear feelings of remorse, or trauma or guilt or distress at having committed those acts. The matter-of-factness is very worrying.

V/O: Forensic psychologist Dr Giada del Fabbro believes the three accused also lack empathy. Hanle Lategan’s murder has had a devastating impact on her husband and family.

Andre: You get up and you think is this the way my life is going to be for the rest of my life? Is this the way I have to continue? It’s hell.

V/O: But the accused were unmoved.

Giada: You don’t care, and you also deny responsibility and culpability in any way. There is also, in terms of psychopathic traits, a lot of lying, so they will believe that in denying they will get away with it.

Devi link: The trial has revealed some bizarre claims made by Cecilia. They’re so laughable it’s like something out of a teenaged vampire movie. But her friends and her accomplices believed every word she said.

Leroux: She told us that she was a 42 generational witch in the Satanic Church, and then when she came out of Satanism then the Satanic church wanted to kill her. This is a werewolf ok? And I got it for Cecilia. She set out and led everybody to believe that she is a werewolf and a vampire with this 42 generational witch thing. And as believing that, I got the werewolf tattoo for her.

Giada: Well I’m not sure how much she bought into that belief, but I do think that individuals like this are quite charismatic and they can be very persuasive, and she sort of exploits it and embroiders that narrative so that the individuals within her circle will actually be quite afraid of the consequences of crossing her.

V/O: This might explain why they managed to keep 6 illegal firearms and hundreds of rounds of ammunition a secret from the police. It was only when Leroux told Captain Ben Booysen about the false compartment in his bedroom cupboard that the weapons were discovered. He also told them about a package of handguns suspended by a rope down the back of the building. And Captain Booysen found a stash of bullets hidden in the ovens of the home economics classroom at Marinda’s school.

Ulrich: The accused do face an uphill battle in this matter; the evidence against them is overwhelming.

Devi: If any of the accused were your clients, would you advise them to testify?

Ulrich: Definitely. In a murder trial if an accused chooses not to testify, a negative inference will be drawn by the Court because that accused must place their version before Court. Otherwise the Court has no option but to accept the evidence that the State has placed on record.

I counted them, in total there over 500 knives. Gerrit: If you look at LLL2, what is depicted on that photograph? Leroux: It is the back of Cecilia’s bedroom door, also be-littered with pangas and machetes and knives and baseball bats, and axes. V/O: Watched by the families, Leroux Steyn testified to Judge Jacob Francis about all the murders. With a deadpan expression he told of the 5 people he personally strangled, beginning with Jarod Jackson. Leroux: There is a piece of rope hanging on that board, a blue piece of rope with some red tape around. Cecilia took that rope off and gave that rope to me and said you are going to be strangling him with this. Zak was driving, Jarod was sitting in the passenger seat, I was sitting behind him because I had to strangle him after he took the medication and passed out. I put the rope over the seat and then I put it around his neck and I pulled tight, while we were driving. We pulled off. After pulling off we took Jarod out of the car and myself and John carried, carried him, dragged him to the Mercedes and put him in the passenger seat of the Mercedes. Myself, Zak and John threw paraffin all over the car on this inside and a bit on the outside. And then we stood away a bit and John set the car on fire. V/O: Leroux’s testimony was corroborated by his partner in crime, convicted murderer John Barnard. John: Zak still put his phone, put it into the driver seat, we moved the body over also into the driver seat, and then we pushed the car off the road. Once we had finished pushing the car off the road, We got paraffin, poured it all over the car and then set it alight. We then left, we went in the opposite direction for about five minutes, turned around and then drove past to make sure that the car is burning alright. Then I let Cecilia know on my phone that we were finished and we were on our way back. Ulrich: The two State witnesses: Leroux Steyn and John Barnard who have testified, I think will be the most important witnesses for the State. Because they can corroborate each other and if they were involved in the murder, then the Defense will have to do a lot in order to disprove those allegations. V/O: Leroux also told the Court why Cecilia needed money so badly, and why they had to keep on killing Leroux: Cecilia was seeing a shrink. Gerrit: A shrink, meaning? A psychologist? Leroux: A psychologist. Ja, paying R5000 a week for her to see the shrink. She started freaking out if she can’t see the shrink, she actually started getting agitated and freaked out, and that amounted to R23 000 a month. Devi link: The testimony of Leroux Steyn and John Barnard has finally lifted the lid on how and why the murders were committed. But for the families of the victims, it’s been difficult to listen to the matter-of-fact telling of their loved ones’ last moments. V/O: Like the description of the murder of Glenn McGregor. Leroux: As he turned to me it looked like he wanted to storm me, and my mother shot him twice in the back, the back, side region. After shooting him he fell to the ground. My mother went into his internet banking, she transferred R6000 from his account to hers. Then my mother told me it’s time now to kill him and that’s, that’s where it happened, where I strangled him. After strangling him, my mother said we can’t leave him in the living room because just now somebody sees him there. So my sister and myself dragged him from the living room all the way to his room in the bathroom, where he was found. Gerrit: Your sister being Accused 3? Leroux: Yes. V/O: The next day Leroux drew the R6000 to give to Cecilia. Leroux: I went and got my mother’s bank card from her while she was at work. I went and drew the money and then I took it to Cecilia. After taking it to Cecilia she sent me to Key West Nedbank to go and pay her shrink. Giada: In his testimony one doesn’t hear feelings of remorse, or trauma or guilt or distress at having committed those acts. The matter-of-factness is very worrying. V/O: Forensic psychologist Dr Giada del Fabbro believes the three accused also lack empathy. Hanle Lategan’s murder has had a devastating impact on her husband and family. Andre: You get up and you think is this the way my life is going to be for the rest of my life? Is this the way I have to continue? It’s hell. V/O: But the accused were unmoved. Giada: You don’t care, and you also deny responsibility and culpability in any way. There is also, in terms of psychopathic traits, a lot of lying, so they will believe that in denying they will get away with it. Devi link: The trial has revealed some bizarre claims made by Cecilia. They’re so laughable it’s like something out of a teenaged vampire movie. But her friends and her accomplices believed every word she said. Leroux: She told us that she was a 42 generational witch in the Satanic Church, and then when she came out of Satanism then the Satanic church wanted to kill her. This is a werewolf ok? And I got it for Cecilia. She set out and led everybody to believe that she is a werewolf and a vampire with this 42 generational witch thing. And as believing that, I got the werewolf tattoo for her. Giada: Well I’m not sure how much she bought into that belief, but I do think that individuals like this are quite charismatic and they can be very persuasive, and she sort of exploits it and embroiders that narrative so that the individuals within her circle will actually be quite afraid of the consequences of crossing her. V/O: This might explain why they managed to keep 6 illegal firearms and hundreds of rounds of ammunition a secret from the police. It was only when Leroux told Captain Ben Booysen about the false compartment in his bedroom cupboard that the weapons were discovered. He also told them about a package of handguns suspended by a rope down the back of the building. And Captain Booysen found a stash of bullets hidden in the ovens of the home economics classroom at Marinda’s school. Ulrich: The accused do face an uphill battle in this matter; the evidence against them is overwhelming. Devi: If any of the accused were your clients, would you advise them to testify? Ulrich: Definitely. In a murder trial if an accused chooses not to testify, a negative inference will be drawn by the Court because that accused must place their version before Court. Otherwise the Court has no option but to accept the evidence that the State has placed on record. metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): The Krugersdorp Killers stand trial for the murder of 11 people
metadata.Unique Selling Point: Exclusive court room footage of the murder trial of a family and three friends who went on a killing spree in Krugersdorp.
metadata.Summary: We bring you the confessions, the testimony, the heartache and legal and psychological analysis of one of the most bizarre murder cases in history. The trial is in its 4th week, but with over 300 witnesses for the prosecution, even the Judge has been asking for time out. What has happened so far? What stunning pieces of evidence have come to light?
metadata.Further information: 1. We begin with a recap of our first story: who was murdered, when and how? Who are the 5 accused, and what were their motives? 2. In June 2018, high school English teacher and mother of two Marinda Steyn pleaded guilty to all 11 murders, and was received 11 life sentences and an additional 115 years in prison. Her confession exonerated her daughter, Marcel, and friend Cecilia Steyn from any involvement in the crimes. 3. In June 2018 her son Leroux Steyn (23) also pleaded guilty to 7 murders and was sentenced to 35 years in prison with 10 suspended for turning state witness. His mother and the rest of the gang have disowned him. 4. In October 2018 Zak Valentine, Cecilia Steyn and Marcel Steyn pleaded not guilty to all charges, and so began the mammoth trial. 5. Leroux Steyn testifies about the Ministry called Electus Per Deus, led by Cecilia Steyn, what was expected and their roles within the group.He gives the Court insight into the motives, planning and execution of all the crimes, including the bombing of cars, selection of victims, their murders, the theft of money and stashing of weapons and ammunition. 6. John Barnard, a member of the gang who was previously sentenced to 25, corroborates Leroux's evidence. He gives insight to his role in the planning and execution of 7 murders. 6. We hear heartbreaking testimony from each of the families about the disappearance and subsequent loss of their loved ones. 7. A trauma counsellor called to the scene of Zak's wife's murder testifies how he showed no emotion at all, and was more concerned about the whereabouts of the cat. 8. Several friends and acquaintances testify about Cecilia Steyn's "special powers" - she is a witch, a werewolf, a vampire, can see auras, and also has several personalities that appear when she is under Satanic attack. 9. A forensic pathologist will unpack these "special powers" and how this manipulation could have influenced the group to commit such heinous crimes.
